A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DriveVA. All 30 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison. Moved and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original planning experiments on NAVSIM, nuScenes and Bench2Drive, together with ablations, DPVO consistency measurements and qualitative failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a preliminary closed-loop Bench2Drive Dev10 comparison in Appendix E.1.

M1.justification: The backbone, joint video-action decoder, conditioning, flow-matching objective and continuation procedure are unchanged. Appendix B's expanded conditioning explanation restates the noise-free context and noisy future targets already specified in Sections 4.3–4.4.

E1.justification: v2 adds an explicitly reported closed-loop route-driving evaluation on Bench2Drive Dev10, extending the existing short-horizon trajectory-transfer evaluations. NAVSIM, nuScenes and Bench2Drive coverage otherwise remains unchanged; no new training domain is introduced.

E2.justification: New Table 10 compares DriveVA with DriveTransformer and DriveMamba-12L on Dev10. Comparator membership in the retained NAVSIM and zero-shot comparisons is unchanged, including PWM and DriveVLA-W0 in Table 2.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 introduces the Dev10 closed-loop protocol with Driving Score and Success Rate. Existing training settings and evaluation metrics are retained. Describing NAVSIM as PDM-based instead of closed-loop does not establish that its experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component, horizon, sampling, training, scaling, masking and action-only ablations are retained, as are the DPVO analyses and failure examples. v1 Table 10 becomes v2 Table 11. The added Dev10 table supplies benchmark results rather than a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new Dev10 results also use point estimates; acknowledging the small split is a limitation, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 10 reports Dev10 Driving Score/Success Rate of 67.47/70.00 for DriveVA, 60.45/30.00 for DriveTransformer and 66.50/40.00 for DriveMamba-12L. All entries in Tables 1–9 and the retained appendix ablation table are unchanged, as are the qualitative examples.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same flow-matching formulation, joint-distribution factorization and reconstruction-error definition. Appendix B revises explanatory prose without adding mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion narrow the NAVSIM claim from state-of-the-art closed-loop performance to PDM-based planning performance. The conclusion also removes the specific long-horizon closed-loop characterization. The joint-generation, continuation and zero-shot-transfer contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits Dev10 evidence to a small diagnostic study that cannot replace full Bench2Drive evaluation. Appendix B adds a leakage-avoidance rationale for conditioning, while Appendix F refines the failure interpretation to distinguish causal or intention-level mistakes from visual artifacts.

D1.justification: v2 removes Appendix H's dataset-source URLs, licensing and usage information. Its shortened ablation explanation also omits the precise causal-attention direction and the explicit distinction between action-only prediction and removing video loss. Core hardware and training hyperparameters remain documented.

R1.justification: The research context is broadly revised across the introduction and related work, with substantial additions across driving, video generation and vision adaptation. Section 2.2 specifically introduces VaViM/VaVAM as a driving VAM precedent, while references including World Action Models Are Zero-Shot Policies, VideoVLA, Hermes and AutoVLA disappear. These changes exceed bibliographic renumbering or publication updates.

P1.justification: Sections 5.4–5.7 and much of the appendix narrative are substantially rewritten or condensed. Appendix B gains a conditioning-interface explanation, Appendix E is reorganized into evaluation and ablation subsections, Appendix F is reframed around limitations, and Appendix H is removed. Acknowledgements and affiliation details are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Dev10 table and relabels the retained appendix ablation table. Existing figures are preserved, with revised captions and placement; Figures 9 and 10 exchange numbering and order. The overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: v2 better bounds its headline NAVSIM claims to PDM-based evidence and adds a clearly qualified Dev10 closed-loop comparison, modestly strengthening the evaluation. These gains outweigh the loss of dataset-access disclosures and precise ablation explanations. The small Dev10 study lacks detailed protocol and uncertainty reporting, while the main results remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
